items.prompt: Which is the best topic sentence for a paragraph about what orangutans eat?

options.text: Orangutans eat mainly fruit, but they also eat leaves, bark and insects.
Orangutans live in Borneo and Sumatra.
options.why: This sentence is about where they live.

options.text: My favourite animal at the zoo is the elephant.
options.why: This is not about orangutans.
This is about their age, not their food.

hints: A topic sentence tells the reader what the whole paragraph is about.
The paragraph is about food.
Find the sentence that mentions what orangutans eat.
items.explanation: A topic sentence introduces the main idea. This one tells the reader that the paragraph is about what orangutans eat.

items.prompt: Choose a connective from the box to fill the gap. Box: However, Therefore, For example. Many people enjoy Car Free Day. ___, some shop owners are unhappy about it.
hints: Read both sentences. Do they agree or contrast?
You need a connective that shows a different side.
Try each connective in the gap and read the two sentences aloud.
items.explanation: However shows a contrast: many people enjoy it, but some shop owners are unhappy.

items.prompt: Match each connective to its job.
pairs: to show something happening at the same time
hints: Connectives link ideas between sentences and paragraphs.
Think of a sentence that could follow each connective.
Start with For example. What usually comes after it?
items.explanation: However contrasts, as a result shows an effect, for example gives an example and meanwhile shows the same time. Finally introduces the last point, and in addition adds another one.

items.prompt: Put the sentences in order to make a clear paragraph.
items: Sea turtles lay their eggs on sandy beaches.
First, the mother digs a deep hole with her back flippers.
Then she lays around a hundred eggs inside it.
After that, she covers the eggs with sand and returns to the sea.
About two months later, the baby turtles hatch and head for the waves.
hints: Look for the topic sentence that introduces the paragraph.
Then use the time connectives: first, then, after that, later.
Start with the sentence that does not begin with a time word.
items.explanation: The topic sentence comes first, then the time connectives First, Then, After that and About two months later put the steps in order.

items.prompt: Which sentence would best begin a new paragraph that moves the story to a different time?

options.why: This describes the parcel but does not move the time on.
This adds a detail. It does not show a change of time.

options.text: Also, the parcel had a label.
options.why: Also adds a detail. It does not show a change of time.

options.text: Three days later, the parcel finally arrived.

hints: New paragraphs often start when the time or place changes.
Look for a phrase that tells the reader when.
Find the sentence that starts with a time phrase.
items.explanation: Three days later tells the reader that time has passed, so it is a good way to start a new paragraph.

items.prompt: Read: Dewi gave Tara her book before she left. Why is this sentence unclear?

options.why: Gave and left are verbs.

options.text: We cannot tell whether her and she mean Dewi or Tara.

options.why: Punctuation is not the problem here.

options.text: Book should have a capital letter.
options.why: Book is a common noun, so it does not need one.

hints: Look at the pronouns her and she.
A pronoun should point clearly to one person.
Ask: whose book was it, and who left?
items.explanation: Her and she could mean either Dewi or Tara. Using a name instead of a pronoun would make the sentence clear.

items.prompt: Paragraph 1 explains why bees are important to farmers. Paragraph 2 describes the dangers bees face. Which sentence best links the two paragraphs?

options.text: Bees are insects with six legs.
options.why: This does not link the two ideas.

options.text: Despite their importance, bees face many dangers.

options.why: This does not link the two ideas.

options.text: In addition, bees are important to farmers.
options.why: This repeats the first paragraph and does not lead into the second.

hints: A good linking sentence looks back and looks forward.
It should mention the idea of paragraph 1 and introduce the idea of paragraph 2.
Find the sentence that mentions both importance and dangers.
items.explanation: Despite their importance looks back to paragraph 1, and bees face many dangers introduces paragraph 2.

items.prompt: Choose all the words and phrases that link ideas across a text.

options.why: Quickly tells us how something is done. It does not link ideas.
Beautiful is an adjective. It does not link ideas.

hints: Linking words connect one idea to another.
They can show results, contrasts or changes in time.
Check each word: does it tell us how two ideas are connected?
items.explanation: Consequently shows a result, on the other hand shows a contrast and later that evening shows a change in time.

items.prompt: Which sentence breaks the flow of this paragraph? (1) Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth. (2) Some kinds grow almost a metre in a day. (3) My cousin plays the flute in a band. (4) Bamboo is used to build houses, furniture and even bicycles.

options.why: This is the topic sentence about bamboo.
This gives evidence for the topic sentence.
This adds more information about bamboo.

hints: Every sentence in a paragraph should be about the same topic.
The topic is given in sentence 1.
Check each sentence: is it about bamboo?
items.explanation: Sentence 3 is about a cousin playing the flute. Every other sentence is about bamboo, so sentence 3 breaks the flow.

items.prompt: Which connective would be wrong in the gap? The bridge was closed. ___, we had to take a longer route.

options.why: Therefore works here: it shows a result.
As a result works here: it shows a result.
Consequently works here: it shows a result.

hints: The second sentence is a result of the first.
Three of the connectives show a result. One shows a contrast.
Look for the connective that means in spite of this.
items.explanation: Nevertheless means in spite of this, so it signals a contrast. Taking a longer route is a result of the closed bridge, not a contrast.
